raw:
**Eight common assumptions, negated**

1. *Assumption:* An edit's value is roughly additive and independent of the other edges. *Negated:* the value depends strongly on a parent edge, so I look for sign flips in the conditional effect.
2. *Assumption:* Replacing "none" with any op gives about the same gain whatever the op. *Negated:* the gain depends on the replaced op, with the largest gain when "none" is replaced and the smallest when skip is replaced. This gives the replacement-specific hypotheses.
3. *Assumption:* A skip on the direct edge 3 helps the whole network, so deeper paths matter less. *Negated:* the skip substitutes for chain upgrades (lower), which gives the edge-3 modulation hypotheses.
4. *Assumption:* A conv on an early edge always helps downstream convs, since features compound. *Negated:* a conv upstream makes later convs redundant, or an upstream pool or skip makes them more valuable.
5. *Assumption:* Avg-pool on an early edge just loses information, so it hurts downstream edits uniformly. *Negated:* a pool feeding an intermediate node lowers the value of downstream conv upgrades, because there is less to refine.
6. *Assumption:* Sibling edges into one node are redundant, like an ensemble. *Negated:* siblings are complementary, so a conv sibling raises the value of another conv. A "none" sibling raises the value of a conv edit, because that edit is then the sole input.
7. *Assumption:* A "none" on a sibling edge is harmful and lowers everything else. *Negated:* a "none" sibling raises the marginal value of the remaining edits at that node.
8. *Assumption:* Op ranking (conv3x3 > conv1x1 > skip > pool) holds the same on every dataset and context. *Negated:* the ranking shifts with the parent, so the interactions are consistent in sign but vary in size. I only keep hypotheses I expect to hold across all three datasets.
